Q2.S025: hierarchical cache allocation + SPILL with paper-claimed ILP/rounding hybrid; useful decomposition but solver visibility, victim-policy consistency and allocator safety require repair
Q2.selection_lesson: separate exact/heuristic paths, post-repair feasibility replay every mapping and centralize victim-selection policy

Visible code computes Mbest/P but does not use them, scalarizes raw Bytes+Cycles, and has a stale globalBestFitness path. Reported extra transfer is higher than S025 on all six workloads, pending common-evaluator verification.
Q2.competition_after_S026: Prefer deterministic lifecycle allocator + spill-cost/next-use baseline first. S025 currently has better reported transfer; S026 contributes reusable feasibility replay and runtime evaluator, not yet a superior optimizer.
Q2.S027: MOACADSA-style First-Fit + dynamic spill/reuse. Reports lower transfer than S025 on five of six workloads, but abstract says Best-Fit, spill argmin math conflicts with reverse-sorted code, and Table 5.11 aggregation is not traceable to Table 5.12.
Q2.competition_after_S027: Use one deterministic lifetime/free-list baseline and one shared evaluator. S027 has promising reported transfer on 5/6 cases, but spill semantics and aggregation must be repaired before promoting it over S025.
Q2.S028: GP/rule-family search plus VN-SA. Useful insight: allocator rule is graph dependent and free-block coalescing matters. But FlashAttention1 final 33792 is not traceable to Table14 min 54720; objective drifts Peak+transfer→Time+transfer and VN-SA defining loop is incomplete.
Q2.final_competition: Robust mainline: lifetime sweep + coalescing free-list + deterministic Best-Fit/linear scan + exact incremental-transfer spill cost; for small active victim sets choose a minimum-cost subset sufficient to free the deficit. GP/hyper-heuristics are high-risk/high-reward and require held-out graph-family validation.

Q3.selection_lesson: hard constraints precede Pareto ranking; return only feasible nondominated solutions and make workload-specific operating-point selection explicit
Q3.S026: DPEA dual-population Pareto narrative. No executable Q3 appendix is visible; Eq.6.67 changes COPY_IN spill cost relative to Q2 and the hard transfer cap is not explicit. Reported improvements relative to S026 Q2 are arithmetically consistent but not implementation-traceable.
Q3.competition_after_S026: Use epsilon-constraint hard-cap baseline as default. DPEA/NSGA-II only after cost semantics are unified and actual feasible Pareto fronts are generated under a common evaluator.
Q3.S027: DOSA/resource-aware scheduling narrative with ~12.62% aggregate cycle reduction and ~7.18% traffic increase; hard cap drifts between 15% and 10%, table signs invert the transfer increase, appendix baseline drifts from Q2 table and optimizer core helper is missing.
Q3.competition_after_S027: Default stays epsilon-constraint: source one official transfer cap, reject infeasible candidates, then minimize cycles. S027 contributes the tolerance-first framing, not yet an executable DOSA implementation.
Q3.S028: Stage1 GP weighted search then NSGA-II/MOPSO Pareto search. Stronger frontier visualization, but 10% cap conflicts with 5% contract candidate, Conv0 baseline is mixed, FlashAttention0 violates stated transfer-first choice and time scales drift.
Q3.final_competition: Robust mainline: canonical epsilon hard cap from original task → feasibility filter → minimize cycles with resource-aware local/LNS search. Pareto NSGA-II/MOPSO only when multiple operating points are required and every point passes the shared evaluator.
